chunks: Ahmad ibn Harun al-Fami (may God be pleased with him) narrated that Muhammad ibn Ja'far ibn Batta said: Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahboob, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Isa, from Muhammad ibn Isma'il ibn Bazee', said: I heard Al-Rida (peace be upon him) say:
Wealth is not accumulated except through five characteristics: extreme stinginess, long hope (for life), overpowering greed, cutting off ties of kinship, and preferring the world over the Hereafter.

key_terms.إِيثَارِ الدُّنْيَا عَلَى الْآخِرَةِ: preferring the world over the Hereafter

ai.seo_question: What are the five characteristics that lead to the accumulation of wealth according to Imam Al-Rida?
ai.summary: Imam Al-Rida (peace be upon him) identifies five key traits that lead to the accumulation of wealth: extreme stinginess, long hope for life, overpowering greed, severing family ties, and prioritizing the worldly life over the Hereafter. This hadith from *Uyun Akhbar al-Rida* highlights the spiritual cost of material accumulation, linking economic behavior to metaphysical priorities. The emphasis on 'severing family ties' (Qati'at al-Rahim) specifically underscores the social dimension of wealth hoarding in Shia ethical tradition.

en.dr-ali-peiravi: 28-13 Ahmad ibn Harun al-Fami - may God be pleased with him - narrated that Muhammad ibn Ja’far ibn Botta quoted on the authority of Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahboob, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Isa, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Isma’il ibn Bazee’, “I heard Al-Ridha (s) say, ‘
Wealth cannot be accumulated unless it is a result of five deeds: extreme jealousy, great aspirations, a lot of greed, cutting off ties of kinship, and preferring this world to the Hereafter.’”
